# @modlin/ui — AI Coding Agent Reference

> Lightweight React UI library built on the Motive design system for consistent, fast, and elegant interfaces.
> This document is the authoritative public-API reference for AI agents writing code against `@modlin/ui`. It covers every exported React component: exact import path, TypeScript props interface, usage examples, and technical constraints. Internal implementation details are intentionally omitted.

---

## 1. Quick Start

### Installation

```bash
npm install @modlin/ui
# or
bun add @modlin/ui
```

Peer dependencies: `next` (^16.2.0), `react` (latest), `react-dom` (latest).

### Global CSS (required)

Import the design tokens once in your app's global stylesheet. The tokens expose the theme colors used by every component (`bg-primary`, `text-foreground`, `inset-ring-border`, etc.) and are theme-aware via `prefers-color-scheme` plus `.light` / `.dark` classes.

```css
/* app/globals.css */
@import "@modlin/ui/globals.css";

@import "tailwindcss";
```

Design tokens provided (Tailwind v4 `@theme` mappings): `background`, `foreground`, `muted`, `muted-foreground`, `border`, `outline`, `priority`, `description`, `disabled`, `primary`, `secondary`, `red`, `yellow`, `green`, `cyan`, `blue`, `magenta`, `purple`, `shadow`, plus `animate-appear`.

### Import pattern — IMPORTANT

There is **no package entry point** (`src/index.ts` does not exist). Every component must be imported via a **subpath export** matching its file name:

```tsx
import Button from "@modlin/ui/button"
import { Accordion, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger, AccordionContent } from "@modlin/ui/accordion"
import { cn } from "@modlin/ui/utils"
```

Rules:
- `@modlin/ui/*` resolves to `src/*.tsx` via the `exports` map. Only the `.tsx` files listed below are importable.
- `@modlin/ui/globals.css` is the only non-component export (CSS tokens).
- Types live alongside components; import them from the same subpath as the component (e.g. `import type { ButtonProps } from "@modlin/ui/button"`).
- Components may be **default exports**, **named exports**, or both — see each section.

### Server Component vs Client Component

- Components marked **"use client"** below bundle React hooks (`useState`, `useEffect`, `useRef`, context) and **must be rendered from a Client Component**. Importing them into a Server Component file causes a Next.js build error.
- Components **without** the directive are server-safe (pure presentational). However, any event-handler props (`onPress`, `onChange`, …) only take effect when the component is used inside a Client Component; event handlers cannot be passed from a Server Component.
- If you need interactivity, add `"use client"` to the file that uses the component (or a wrapper component).

### Shared base types (`src/globals.ts`)

Used by most component prop interfaces:

```ts
export type Variant = "primary" | "secondary" | "destructive" | "outline" | "ghost" | "link" | "none"
export type Size = "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | "icon" | "none"
export type Shape = "square" | "rounded" | "pill"

export interface ViewProps {
  /** @platform android, ios, web */
  children?: ReactNode
  /** @platform android, ios, web */
  style?: CSSProperties
  /** @platform web */
  className?: string
}
```

### Utilities (`src/utils.ts`)

```ts
import { cn, mergeProps } from "@modlin/ui/utils"

cn(...inputs)                                  // clsx + tailwind-merge (re-exported from "cnfast")
mergeProps(childProps, parentProps)            // shallow-merge; parent wins unless value is undefined
```

---

## 2. Layout & Structure

### `Card` — Layout container

- **Import:** `import Card, { CardHeader, CardContent, CardFooter, CardAction } from "@modlin/ui/card"` (named + default)
- **Constraints:** Server-safe. Renders `<article>` (Card), `<header>`, `<div>`, `<footer>`. No hooks, no directives.

**Props**

```ts
export interface CardProps extends ViewProps {
  size?: "md" | "lg" | "xl"   // default "md"; md = p-4 rounded-2xl, lg = p-6, xl = p-8 rounded-4xl
}
// CardHeader, CardContent, CardFooter, CardAction all extend ViewProps (empty additions)
```

**Example**

```tsx
// app/page.tsx  (Server Component)
import Card, { CardHeader, CardContent, CardFooter } from "@modlin/ui/card"
import Button from "@modlin/ui/button"
import { Heading2 } from "@modlin/ui/heading"

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <Card size="lg" className="max-w-md">
      <CardHeader>
        <Heading2 className="text-start">Account settings</Heading2>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardContent className="flex-col gap-4">
        <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Manage your profile details.</p>
      </CardContent>
      <CardFooter>
        <Button variant="primary" size="md" shape="rounded">Save changes</Button>
      </CardFooter>
    </Card>
  )
}
```

---

### `Stack` / `VStack` / `HStack` — Flexbox layout primitives

- **Import:** `import Stack, { VStack, HStack } from "@modlin/ui/stack"`
- **Constraints:** Server-safe. `Stack` renders a flex column (`flex flex-col`); `HStack` renders `flex` (row). Sizes are applied via inline `style`, not Tailwind classes.

**Props**

```ts
interface StackProps {
  align?: "start" | "center" | "end"      // alignItems (inline style)
  justify?: "start" | "center" | "end"    // justifyContent (inline style)
  gap?: number                            // gap in px (inline style)
  direction?: "uphold" | "reverse"        // NOTE: accepted but NOT applied in the implementation
  children: React.ReactNode
  className?: string
  style?: CSSProperties
}
```

**Example**

```tsx
// app/page.tsx (Server Component)
import { VStack, HStack } from "@modlin/ui/stack"
import Text from "@modlin/ui/text"

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <VStack gap={16} align="center">
      <Text>Name</Text>
      <HStack justify="center" gap={8}>
        <Text>React</Text>
        <Text>Next.js</Text>
      </HStack>
    </VStack>
  )
}
```

---

### `View` / `ScrollView` / `FlatList` / `Stack` — Low-level layout

- **Import:** `import View, { ScrollView, FlatList, Stack } from "@modlin/ui/view"` (default `View`)
- **Constraints:** Server-safe. React-Native-inspired aliases over plain HTML. Note the `Stack` in this file is distinct from `@modlin/ui/stack`. Renders `<div>` / `<ul>` / `<li>`.

**Props**

```ts
export interface ViewProps {
  children?: ReactNode
  style?: CSSProperties
  className?: string
}

export interface StackProps extends ViewProps {
  alignment?: "leading" | "trailing"   // NOTE: declared but not applied
  spacing?: number                     // NOTE: declared but not applied
}

export interface ScrollViewProps extends ViewProps {}   // renders overflow-y-auto flex-col div

export interface FlatListProps<ItemT> extends ViewProps {
  data: ItemT[]
  draggable?: boolean
  renderItem(item: { item: ItemT; index: number }): JSX.Element | null
  keyExtractor?: (item: ItemT, index: number) => string
  ItemSeparatorComponent?: JSX.Element | React.FC
  ListFooterComponent?: JSX.Element | React.FC
}
```

**Example**

```tsx
// app/page.tsx (Server Component)
import { FlatList } from "@modlin/ui/view"

type Row = { id: string; title: string }

export default function Page() {
  const rows: Row[] = [
    { id: "1", title: "First" },
    { id: "2", title: "Second" },
  ]
  return (
    <FlatList<Row>
      data={rows}
      keyExtractor={r => r.id}
      renderItem={({ item }) => <p>{item.title}</p>}
    />
  )
}
```

---

### `Content` — Generic content wrapper

- **Import:** `import Content from "@modlin/ui/content"`
- **Constraints:** Server-safe. Renders `<div className="flex">`.

**Props**

```ts
export interface ContentProps {
  children: React.ReactNode   // required
  className?: string
}
```

**Example**

```tsx
import Content from "@modlin/ui/content"

<Content className="max-w-prose flex-col gap-4">
  <p>Body content</p>
</Content>
```

---

### `Footer` — Generic footer wrapper

- **Import:** `import Footer from "@modlin/ui/footer"`
- **Constraints:** Server-safe. Renders `<div className="flex">`.

**Props**

```ts
export interface FooterProps {
  children: React.ReactNode   // required
  className?: string
}
```

---

### `Header` — Section header composed of a Heading + Text

- **Import:** `import Header from "@modlin/ui/header"`
- **Constraints:** Server-safe. `children` must be exactly a two-element tuple: `[Heading, Text]` (enforced by the prop type).

**Props**

```ts
export interface HeaderProps {
  gap?: number                                    // default 8 (px)
  children: [ReactElement<HeadingProps>, ReactElement<TextProps>]  // required tuple
  className?: string
}
```

**Example**

```tsx
import Header from "@modlin/ui/header"
import { Heading2 } from "@modlin/ui/heading"
import Text from "@modlin/ui/text"

<Header gap={12}>
  <Heading2>Documentation</Heading2>
  <Text className="text-muted-foreground">Guides for using the library.</Text>
</Header>
```

---

### `Separator` — Horizontal/vertical rule

- **Import:** `import Separator from "@modlin/ui/separator"`
- **Constraints:** Server-safe. Renders `<hr>`. Preferred over the deprecated `Divider`.

**Props**

```ts
export interface SeparatorProps {
  className?: string
  orientation?: "vertical" | "horizontal"   // default "horizontal"
}
```

**Example**

```tsx
import Separator from "@modlin/ui/separator"

<div className="flex h-10 items-center gap-4">
  <span>Left</span>
  <Separator orientation="vertical" />
  <span>Right</span>
</div>
```

---

### `Divider` — ⚠️ Deprecated

- **Import:** `import Divider from "@modlin/ui/divider"`
- **Constraints:** **Deprecated** (JSDoc `@deprecated`). Renders `<div>` with `data-orientation`. Use `Separator` instead.

**Props**

```ts
export interface DividerProps {
  className?: string
  orientation?: "vertical" | "horizontal"
}
```

## 3. Typography

### `Heading` / `Heading1`…`Heading6`

- **Import:** `import Heading, { Heading1, Heading2, Heading3, Heading4, Heading5, Heading6 } from "@modlin/ui/heading"`
- **Constraints:** Server-safe. Default export `Heading` is an alias of `Heading1` (renders `<h1>`). All render semantic heading tags with shadcn-style styling; the `first` prop is consumed by the `first:` variants internally via the class string.

**Props**

```ts
export interface HeadingProps {
  first?: boolean
  children?: React.ReactNode
  className?: string
}
```

**Example**

```tsx
import { Heading1, Heading2, Heading3 } from "@modlin/ui/heading"

<>
  <Heading1>Page title</Heading1>
  <Heading2>Section</Heading2>
  <Heading3>Sub-section</Heading3>
</>
```

---

### `Text`

- **Import:** `import Text from "@modlin/ui/text"`
- **Constraints:** Server-safe. Renders `<p>`.

**Props**

```ts
export interface TextProps {
  className?: string
  style?: CSSProperties
  children?: ReactNode
}
```

---

### Typography presets (`src/typography.tsx`)

- **Import:** `import { InlineCode, Lead, Large, Small, Muted, Caption } from "@modlin/ui/typography"`
- **Constraints:** Server-safe. All components are `forwardRef`-enabled and accept `children` + `className` only.

**Props**

```ts
export interface TypographyProps {
  children?: ReactNode
  className?: string
}
```

| Component | Renders | Default styling |
|---|---|---|
| `InlineCode` | `<code>` | `bg-muted` mono, `rounded` |
| `Lead` | `<p>` | `text-xl text-muted-foreground` |
| `Large` | `<div>` | `text-lg font-semibold` |
| `Small` | `<small>` | `text-sm leading-none font-medium` |
| `Muted` | `<p>` | `text-sm text-muted-foreground` |
| `Caption` | `<p>` | `text-xs text-muted-foreground select-none` |

**Example**

```tsx
import { InlineCode, Lead, Muted, Small, Caption, Large } from "@modlin/ui/typography"

<>
  <Lead>Introduction to the design system.</Lead>
  <Muted>Secondary explanation text.</Muted>
  <Small>Legal fine print.</Small>
  <Caption>Photo caption.</Caption>
  <Large>Highlighted value</Large>
  <p>Run <InlineCode>npm install</InlineCode> to begin.</p>
</>
```

---

### `Kbd` / `KbdGroup`

- **Import:** `import Kbd, { KbdGroup } from "@modlin/ui/kbd"` (default `Kbd`)
- **Constraints:** Server-safe. Renders `<kbd>` (uses `font-icons` class — the icon font glyph is the character placed inside).

**Props**

```ts
// Kbd and KbdGroup both accept ViewProps
export interface ViewProps {
  children?: ReactNode
  style?: CSSProperties
  className?: string
}
```

**Example**

```tsx
import Kbd, { KbdGroup } from "@modlin/ui/kbd"

<KbdGroup>
  <Kbd>⌘</Kbd>
  <Kbd>K</Kbd>
</KbdGroup>
```

---

## 4. Forms & Inputs

### `TextInput` — Text/email/number/etc. input

- **Import:** `import TextInput, { Prompt, InputGroup, textInputVariants } from "@modlin/ui/input"` (default + named)
- **Constraints:** Server-safe. Renders `<input>`. `onChangeText` and `onChange` are mutually exclusive — when `onChangeText` is provided it wins and passes the raw string; otherwise `onChange` receives the full `ChangeEvent`. Styling variants are built with `cva` and exported as `textInputVariants`.

**Props**

```ts
export interface TextInputProps extends VariantProps<typeof textInputVariants> {
  // cva variants — default variant "primary", size "xl"
  variant?: "primary" | "secondary" | "destructive" | "none"
  size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | "none"
  shape?: "square" | "rounded" | "pill"

  placeholder?: string
  defaultValue?: string
  value?: string
  inputMode?: "search" | "text" | "email" | "tel" | "url" | "none" | "numeric" | "decimal"
  autoCapitalize?: "none" | "sentences" | "words" | "characters"
  autoComplete?: HTMLInputAutoCompleteAttribute
  autoCorrect?: boolean              // true → "on", else "off"
  autoFocus?: boolean
  readOnly?: boolean
  maxLength?: number
  id?: string
  type?: "text" | "password" | "email" | "number" | "tel" | "url" | "file"  // default "text"
  name?: string
  required?: boolean
  disabled?: boolean
  pattern?: string
  min?: number | string
  max?: number | string
  minLength?: number
  invalid?: boolean                  // sets data-invalid → red ring styling
  describedby?: string              // aria-describedby
  className?: string

  onChange?(event: ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>): void
  onChangeText?(text: string): void
  onFocus?(event: FocusEvent<HTMLInputElement>): void
  onBlur?(event: FocusEvent<HTMLInputElement>): void
  onInvalid?(event: InvalidEvent<HTMLInputElement>): void
}
```

**Example**

```tsx
// app/components/email-form.tsx ("use client")
import TextInput from "@modlin/ui/input"
import Label from "@modlin/ui/label"
import Button from "@modlin/ui/button"
import { useState } from "react"

export default function EmailForm() {
  const [email, setEmail] = useState("")
  return (
    <form className="flex flex-col gap-4">
      <Label htmlFor="email">Email</Label>
      <TextInput
        id="email"
        type="email"
        size="md"
        placeholder="you@example.com"
        value={email}
        onChangeText={setEmail}
        required
      />
      <Button type="submit" size="md" shape="rounded">Subscribe</Button>
    </form>
  )
}
```

**Related exports in `@modlin/ui/input`**

- `Prompt(props)` — a `TextInput` with `variant="none" size="none"` (unstyled, for building custom inputs).
- `InputGroup(props: InputGroupProps)` — a `<span>` carrying the same variant styling, for prefix/suffix content around an input (e.g. icons, currency symbols). `InputGroupProps extends TextInputProps { children?: ReactNode }`.
- ⚠️ There is a separate empty file `src/input-group.tsx` with **no exports** — do not import from `@modlin/ui/input-group`; use `InputGroup` from `@modlin/ui/input`.
- `textInputVariants` — the underlying `cva` recipe.

---

### `Textarea`

- **Import:** `import Textarea from "@modlin/ui/textarea"`
- **Constraints:** Server-safe. Renders `<textarea>`. `onChange` receives the raw string value (not an event). `variant` is declared in the props but **not applied** in the implementation.

**Props**

```ts
export interface TextareaProps {
  type?: "text" | "password" | "email" | "number" | "tel" | "url" | "file"
  disabled?: boolean
  placeholder?: string
  value?: string
  maxLength?: number
  minLength?: number
  required?: boolean
  name?: string
  id?: string
  onChange?: (value: string) => void
  width?: number | string
  size?: "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl"   // default "xl" (min-h-12 rounded-2xl px-4 py-3)
  variant?: "primary" | "secondary" | "none" // declared but not applied
  className?: string
}
```

**Example**

```tsx
// app/components/feedback-form.tsx ("use client")
import Textarea from "@modlin/ui/textarea"
import { useState } from "react"

export default function FeedbackForm() {
  const [message, setMessage] = useState("")
  return (
    <Textarea
      placeholder="Write your feedback…"
      value={message}
      onChange={setMessage}
      maxLength={500}
      size="sm"
    />
  )
}
```

---

### `Checkbox` — ⚠️ "use client"

- **Import:** `import Checkbox from "@modlin/ui/checkbox"`
- **Constraints:** **"use client"** — uses `useRef`. Renders a hidden native `<input type="checkbox">` paired with a styled `<button role="checkbox">`. State must be wired through `onChange` (the visual state is driven by the hidden peer input). `value` and `onValueChange` are **deprecated** — use `checked` / `onChange`.

**Props**

```ts
export interface CheckboxProps {
  disabled?: boolean
  defaultChecked?: boolean
  checked?: boolean
  label?: string               // used as aria-label
  required?: boolean
  name?: string
  id?: string
  asChild?: boolean
  onChange?(checked: boolean): void

  /** @deprecated @use checked */
  value?: string
  /** @deprecated @use onChange */
  onValueChange?(event: ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>): void
}
```

**Example**

```tsx
// app/components/terms.tsx ("use client")
import Checkbox from "@modlin/ui/checkbox"
import { useState } from "react"

export default function TermsCheckbox() {
  const [accepted, setAccepted] = useState(false)
  return (
    <Checkbox
      label="I accept the terms"
      checked={accepted}
      onChange={setAccepted}
    />
  )
}
```

---

### `Switch` — ⚠️ "use client"

- **Import:** `import Switch from "@modlin/ui/switch"`
- **Constraints:** **"use client"** — uses `useState`/`useEffect`. Renders a hidden native `<input type="checkbox">` paired with a styled `<button role="switch">`. Controlled via `checked` / `onChange` (the effect re-fires `onChange` whenever the internal state changes). ⚠️ Quirk: the hidden input uses `name={props.id}` instead of `props.name`.

**Props**

```ts
export interface SwitchProps {
  checked?: boolean
  onChange?(checked: boolean): void
  disabled?: boolean
  size?: "sm" | "lg"          // default "lg"
  label?: string              // used as aria-label
  required?: boolean          // web
  name?: string               // web — NOTE: not actually applied (input uses id)
  value?: string              // web
  id?: string                 // web
}
```

**Example**

```tsx
// app/components/notifications.tsx ("use client")
import Switch from "@modlin/ui/switch"
import { useState } from "react"

export default function Notifications() {
  const [enabled, setEnabled] = useState(true)
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
      <span>Email notifications</span>
      <Switch size="sm" checked={enabled} onChange={setEnabled} />
    </div>
  )
}
```

---

### `RadioGroup` / `RadioGroupItem`

- **Import:** `import { RadioGroup, RadioGroupItem } from "@modlin/ui/radio"`
- **Constraints:** Server-safe. Thin wrappers over native HTML: `<fieldset>` + `<input type="radio">`. Shared `name` must be set manually on both or on the group. Note the group's default prop is `default` (not `defaultValue`).

**Props**

```ts
export interface RadioGroupProps {
  default?: string
  name?: string
  required?: boolean
  children: React.ReactNode
}

export interface RadioGroupItemProps {
  value: string        // required
  name?: string
  id?: string
}
```

**Example**

```tsx
// app/components/fruit-picker.tsx (Server Component)
import { RadioGroup, RadioGroupItem } from "@modlin/ui/radio"
import Label from "@modlin/ui/label"

<RadioGroup name="fruit" default="apple" required>
  <Label htmlFor="apple">
    <RadioGroupItem value="apple" id="apple" name="fruit" /> Apple
  </Label>
  <Label htmlFor="banana">
    <RadioGroupItem value="banana" id="banana" name="fruit" /> Banana
  </Label>
</RadioGroup>
```

---

### `Select` + `SelectItem` (native) — `src/select.native.tsx`

- **Import:** `import { Select, SelectItem } from "@modlin/ui/select.native"`
- **Constraints:** Server-safe. Renders native `<select>` / `<option>` and relies on the base-select styling in `globals.css` (fancy animated picker). Styling via `cva` (`selectVariants`).

**Props**

```ts
export interface SelectProps extends ViewProps, VariantProps<typeof selectVariants> {
  defaultValue?: string
  value?: string
  onChange?: (event: ChangeEvent<HTMLSelectElement>) => void
  name?: string
  id?: string
  // cva variants — default variant "primary", size "xl"
  variant?: "primary" | "secondary" | "none"
  size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | "none"
}

export interface SelectItemProps {
  disabled?: boolean
  selected?: boolean
  hidden?: boolean
  value: string      // required
  children?: ReactNode
  className?: string
}
```

**Example**

```tsx
// app/components/country-select.tsx (Server Component)
import { Select, SelectItem } from "@modlin/ui/select.native"
import Label from "@modlin/ui/label"

<>
  <Label htmlFor="country">Country</Label>
  <Select id="country" name="country" size="md" defaultValue="us">
    <SelectItem value="us">United States</SelectItem>
    <SelectItem value="de">Germany</SelectItem>
    <SelectItem value="jp">Japan</SelectItem>
  </Select>
</>
```

---

### `Select` (custom dropdown) — ⚠️ "use client", in-progress

- **Import:** `import { Select, SelectTrigger, SelectContent, SelectItem, Dropdown } from "@modlin/ui/select"`
- **Constraints:** **"use client"** — uses `useState` and `React.Children.cloneElement` to wire item selection. This is an early/experimental implementation (open/close is manually managed, no outside-click handling, hardcoded `max-w-56`, placeholder required). Prefer the native `@modlin/ui/select.native` for production use.

**Props**

```ts
export interface SelectProps {
  defaultValue?: string
  placeholder: string           // required
  value?: string
  name?: string
  id?: string
  children: ReactElement<SelectItemProps>[]   // required
}

export interface SelectTriggerProps {
  placeholder?: string
  id?: string
  children?: string
}

export interface SelectContentProps {
  defaultValue: string        // required
  children?: ReactNode
}

export interface SelectItemProps {
  value: string               // required
  children: ReactNode
  className?: string
  onPress?: () => void        // auto-injected by Select/SelectContent
}
```

**Example**

```tsx
// app/components/gender-select.tsx ("use client")
import { Select, SelectItem } from "@modlin/ui/select"

export default function GenderSelect() {
  return (
    <Select placeholder="Select a gender">
      <SelectItem value="male">Male</SelectItem>
      <SelectItem value="female">Female</SelectItem>
      <SelectItem value="other">Other</SelectItem>
    </Select>
  )
}
```

---

### `PasswordField` — ⚠️ "use client"

- **Import:** `import PasswordField from "@modlin/ui/password"`
- **Constraints:** **"use client"** — uses `useState` for the show/hide toggle. Extends `TextInputProps` and forces `autoCapitalize="none"` and `autoComplete="current-password"`. Any `children` render after the input inside the wrapper.

**Props**

```ts
export interface PasswordFieldProps extends TextInputProps {
  children?: ReactNode
}
// (see TextInputProps in the TextInput section above for the inherited fields)
```

**Example**

```tsx
// app/components/login-form.tsx ("use client")
import PasswordField from "@modlin/ui/password"
import TextInput from "@modlin/ui/input"
import Label from "@modlin/ui/label"
import Button from "@modlin/ui/button"

export default function LoginForm() {
  return (
    <form className="flex flex-col gap-4">
      <Label htmlFor="email">Email</Label>
      <TextInput id="email" type="email" size="md" placeholder="you@example.com" />
      <Label htmlFor="password">Password</Label>
      <PasswordField id="password" size="md" placeholder="••••••••" />
      <Button type="submit" size="md" shape="rounded">Sign in</Button>
    </form>
  )
}
```

---

### `Label`

- **Import:** `import Label from "@modlin/ui/label"`
- **Constraints:** Server-safe. Renders `<label>`. `htmlFor` and `children` are required. With `asChild`, the label props are merged onto the child element (e.g. to wrap a `RadioGroupItem`).

**Props**

```ts
export interface LabelProps {
  htmlFor: string        // required
  label?: string         // used as aria-label
  children: ReactNode    // required
  className?: string
  onPress?: React.MouseEventHandler<HTMLLabelElement>
  asChild?: boolean
}
```

**Example**

```tsx
import Label from "@modlin/ui/label"

<Label htmlFor="name" className="text-sm font-medium">Full name</Label>
```

---

### `ErrorMessage`

- **Import:** `import { ErrorMessage } from "@modlin/ui/errormessage"`
- **Constraints:** Server-safe. Renders a red `<Small>`; returns `undefined` (renders nothing) when `children` is falsy — safe to always render conditionally. Default icon is the glyph `"\uea05"` unless overridden.

**Props**

```ts
export interface ErrorMessageProps {
  icon?: ReactNode
  children?: ReactNode
  id?: string
  className?: string
}
```

**Example**

```tsx
// app/components/signup-form.tsx ("use client")
import { ErrorMessage } from "@modlin/ui/errormessage"
import { IconAlertTriangle } from "@tabler/icons-react"

<ErrorMessage icon={<IconAlertTriangle />} id="email-error">
  Please enter a valid email address.
</ErrorMessage>
```

---

## 5. Feedback & Status

### `Alert` / `AlertTitle` / `AlertDescription`

- **Import:** `import { Alert, AlertTitle, AlertDescription } from "@modlin/ui/alert"`
- **Constraints:** Server-safe. Composes via a grid layout: children are expected as an icon (16px) followed by `AlertTitle` and `AlertDescription`. `dismissible` is declared in `AlertProps` but **not implemented**. `Alert.Destructive` is a static alternate variant (red text).

**Props**

```ts
export interface AlertProps extends ViewProps {
  dismissible?: boolean    // declared but not implemented
}
// AlertTitleProps, AlertDescriptionProps extend ViewProps (empty)
```

**Example**

```tsx
import { Alert, AlertTitle, AlertDescription } from "@modlin/ui/alert"
import { IconInfoCircle } from "@tabler/icons-react"

<Alert>
  <IconInfoCircle size={16} className="text-muted-foreground" />
  <AlertTitle>Heads up</AlertTitle>
  <AlertDescription>Your account is being reviewed.</AlertDescription>
</Alert>

<Alert.Destructive className="mt-4">
  <IconX size={16} />
  <AlertTitle>Access denied</AlertTitle>
  <AlertDescription>You do not have permission.</AlertDescription>
</Alert.Destructive>
```

---

### `Badge`

- **Import:** `import Badge from "@modlin/ui/badge"`
- **Constraints:** Server-safe. Renders `<span>`. When `children` is a `number`, a fixed `w-5` width is applied (count badge).

**Props**

```ts
export interface BadgeProps {
  variant?: "primary" | "secondary" | "destructive" | "outline"  // default "primary"
  size?: "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg"                               // default "md"
  shape?: "square" | "rounded" | "pill"                          // default "pill"
  children?: ReactNode | number
  className?: string
}
```

**Example**

```tsx
import Badge from "@modlin/ui/badge"

<Badge variant="secondary" size="sm">beta</Badge>
<Badge variant="destructive">{3}</Badge>
```

---

### `Skeleton`

- **Import:** `import { Skeleton } from "@modlin/ui/skeleton"`
- **Constraints:** Server-safe. Renders a `<div>` with `animate-pulse bg-muted rounded-lg`. Width/height must be supplied via `className` or it collapses (no intrinsic size).

**Props**

```ts
export interface SkeletonProps {
  className?: string
}
```

**Example**

```tsx
import { Skeleton } from "@modlin/ui/skeleton"

<div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
  <Skeleton className="h-4 w-1/2" />
  <Skeleton className="h-10 w-full" />
</div>
```

---

### `Spinner`

- **Import:** `import Spinner from "@modlin/ui/spinner"`
- **Constraints:** Server-safe. Renders `IconLoader2` from `@tabler/icons-react` with `animate-spin`, `role="status"`, `aria-label="Loading..."`. Accepts any SVG props.

**Props**

```ts
// Spinner accepts React.SVGProps (React.ComponentProps<"svg">)
{ className?: string; ...rest }
```

**Example**

```tsx
import Spinner from "@modlin/ui/spinner"

<Spinner className="size-5 text-primary" />
```

---

### `Tooltip`

- **Import:** `import Tooltip from "@modlin/ui/tooltip"`
- **Constraints:** Server-safe. CSS-only hover tooltip (uses `group-hover`). The label is rendered inside a `Badge`. `label` is required.

**Props**

```ts
export interface TooltipProps {
  label: string      // required
  className?: string // applied to the tooltip badge
  children?: ReactNode
}
```

**Example**

```tsx
import Tooltip from "@modlin/ui/tooltip"
import Button from "@modlin/ui/button"

<Tooltip label="Copy link">
  <Button size="icon-sm" shape="rounded" variant="outline">🔗</Button>
</Tooltip>
```

---

### `Copy` — ⚠️ "use client"

- **Import:** `import Copy from "@modlin/ui/copy"` (named + default)
- **Constraints:** **"use client"** — uses `navigator.clipboard.writeText`. Wraps `Button` (internally sets `variant="none" size="none"`, then spreads your props on top, so you can still pass any `ButtonProps`). Requires a secure context (HTTPS or localhost) for the Clipboard API. Calls `onCopy` / `onStatusChange` after the write.

**Props**

```ts
export type CopyStatus = "success" | "failed" | "none"

export interface CopyProps extends ButtonProps {
  copy?: string
  copied?: boolean
  onCopy?: (copied: boolean) => void | Promise<void>
  onStatusChange?: (status: CopyStatus) => void | Promise<void>
}
// (see ButtonProps in the Button section below for inherited fields)
```

**Example**

```tsx
// app/components/code-block.tsx ("use client")
import Copy from "@modlin/ui/copy"
import { useState } from "react"

export default function CodeBlock({ code }: { code: string }) {
  const [status, setStatus] = useState<"none" | "success" | "failed">("none")
  return (
    <Copy
      copy={code}
      size="sm"
      variant="outline"
      shape="rounded"
      onStatusChange={setStatus}
    >
      {status === "success" ? "Copied!" : "Copy"}
    </Copy>
  )
}
```

---

### `toast` — ⚠️ Client-only function

- **Import:** `import { toast } from "@modlin/ui/toast"`
- **Constraints:** **Client-only** — directly manipulates `document`. It appends a `<div>` into an element with `id="toasts"`, so your app must include a `#toasts` mount point. The `description` option is declared but **not used** by the implementation. Only one toast is supported at a time (no queue).

**Props**

```ts
export interface ToastOptions {
  description?: string   // declared but not used
}
export function toast(title: string, _options?: ToastOptions): false
```

**Example**

```tsx
// app/layout.tsx — add the mount point once
export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html>
      <body>
        {children}
        <div id="toasts" className="fixed inset-x-0 top-0 flex flex-col items-center gap-2" />
      </body>
    </html>
  )
}

// app/components/save.tsx ("use client")
import { toast } from "@modlin/ui/toast"

export function SaveButton() {
  return <button onClick={() => toast("Settings saved")}>Save</button>
}
```

---

## 6. Navigation & Interactive

### `Button`

- **Import:** `import Button, { buttonVariants, type ButtonProps } from "@modlin/ui/button"`
- **Constraints:** Server-safe (no hooks). Renders `<button>`; when `loading` is true the button is disabled and renders a `Spinner`. `label` maps to both `aria-label` and `title`. `asChild` clones the given child and merges button behavior onto it (e.g. a `next/link`). Variants are exposed as `buttonVariants` (a `cva` recipe) for reuse.

**Props**

```ts
export interface ButtonProps extends ViewProps, VariantProps<typeof buttonVariants> {
  // cva variants — default variant "primary", size "xl", shape "pill"
  variant?: "primary" | "secondary" | "destructive" | "outline" | "ghost" | "link" | "none"
  size?: "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | "icon" | "icon-xs" | "icon-sm" | "icon-md" | "none"
  shape?: "square" | "rounded" | "pill"

  disabled?: boolean
  loading?: boolean            // disables + shows Spinner
  label?: string               // aria-label + title
  title?: string               // rendered text (overrides children when set)
  asChild?: boolean            // merge behavior onto a single child element
  haptics?: boolean            // @android @ios — no-op on web
  full?: boolean               // @android @ios — no-op on web
  rounded?: number             // @android @ios — no-op on web
  id?: string
  type?: "button" | "reset" | "submit"   // default "button"
  popoverTarget?: string

  onPress?(event: MouseEvent): void | Promise<void>       // → onClick
  onPressIn?(event: MouseEvent): void | Promise<void>     // → onMouseDown
  onPressOut?(event: MouseEvent): void | Promise<void>    // → onMouseUp
  onMouseEnter?(event: MouseEvent): void | Promise<void>
  onMouseLeave?(event: MouseEvent): void | Promise<void>
  onHover?(event: MouseEvent): void | Promise<void>       // → onMouseOver
  onFocus?(event: FocusEvent): void | Promise<void>
  onBlur?(event: FocusEvent): void | Promise<void>
}
```

**Example**

```tsx
// app/components/cta.tsx ("use client" — needs onPress)
import Button from "@modlin/ui/button"
import { IconArrowRight } from "@tabler/icons-react"

export function CtaButton() {
  return (
    <Button
      variant="primary"
      size="xl"
      shape="pill"
      label="Get started"
      onPress={async () => console.log("clicked")}
    >
      Get started
      <IconArrowRight />
    </Button>
  )
}
```

**As-child with a Next link:**

```tsx
// app/components/link-button.tsx (Server Component — static rendering)
import Button from "@modlin/ui/button"
import Link from "next/link"

export function LinkButton() {
  return (
    <Button asChild variant="secondary" size="md" shape="rounded">
      <Link href="/docs">Read the docs</Link>
    </Button>
  )
}
```

---

### `Link` — ⚠️ "use client"

- **Import:** `import Link from "@modlin/ui/link"`
- **Constraints:** **"use client"** — uses `useState` for copy feedback. Wraps **Next.js `<Link>`** (`next/link`), so all `next/link` props pass through (`href` is required). Default styling is `text-primary/75 hover:underline hover:text-primary`. Passing `copyable` (or `copy`) adds a hover-revealed copy button that writes `copy ?? href` to the clipboard. ⚠️ This component is named `Link`; do not confuse it with `next/link` — import the UI version from `@modlin/ui/link`.

**Props**

```ts
export interface LinkProps extends LinkProps /* next/link */ {
  copy?: string
  className?: string
  children?: ReactNode
  copyable?: boolean
}
```

**Example**

```tsx
// app/components/doc-link.tsx ("use client")
import Link from "@modlin/ui/link"

export default function DocLink() {
  return (
    <Link href="https://example.com/docs" copyable>
      Read documentation
    </Link>
  )
}
```

---

### `Item`

- **Import:** `import Item from "@modlin/ui/item"` (named + default)
- **Constraints:** Server-safe. Renders `<li>`. With `asChild`, merges item styling (padding, hover, icon sizing) onto the child element.

**Props**

```ts
export interface ItemProps extends ViewProps {
  asChild?: boolean
}
```

**Example**

```tsx
import Item from "@modlin/ui/item"
import { IconSettings } from "@tabler/icons-react"

<ul>
  <Item className="items-center">
    <IconSettings />
    <span>Settings</span>
  </Item>
</ul>
```

---

### `Pagination`

- **Import:** `import { Pagination, PaginationContent, PaginationItem, PaginationLink, PaginationButton, PaginationPrevious, PaginationNext, PaginationEllipsis } from "@modlin/ui/pagination"`
- **Constraints:** Server-safe. Composite component built on `Button` + `next/link`. `PaginationLink` renders a `Button` (`asChild`) wrapping a `next/link` — `href` is required and `isActive` swaps to the `secondary` variant. `PaginationPrevious` / `PaginationNext` use icon chevrons (note: Next's default `aria-label` says "Go to previous page" — a copy-paste quirk in the library).

**Props**

```ts
export interface PaginationProps extends ViewProps {}            // <nav aria-label="pagination">
export interface PaginationContentProps extends ViewProps {}     // <ul>
export interface PaginationItemProps extends ViewProps {}        // <ul> (quirk: renders ul)
export interface PaginationLinkProps extends ViewProps {
  isActive?: boolean
}
// PaginationLink accepts LinkProps (next/link) + ButtonProps as well
export interface PaginationButtonProps extends ButtonProps {
  isActive?: boolean
}
export interface PaginationPreviousProps extends PaginationButtonProps {}
export interface PaginationNextProps extends PaginationButtonProps {}
export interface PaginationEllipsisProps extends ViewProps {}   // <span aria-hidden>
```

**Example**

```tsx
import {
  Pagination, PaginationContent, PaginationItem, PaginationLink,
  PaginationPrevious, PaginationNext, PaginationEllipsis,
} from "@modlin/ui/pagination"

<Pagination>
  <PaginationContent>
    <PaginationItem>
      <PaginationPrevious href="/page/2" />
    </PaginationItem>
    <PaginationItem>
      <PaginationLink href="/page/1">1</PaginationLink>
    </PaginationItem>
    <PaginationItem>
      <PaginationLink href="/page/2" isActive>2</PaginationLink>
    </PaginationItem>
    <PaginationItem>
      <PaginationEllipsis />
    </PaginationItem>
    <PaginationItem>
      <PaginationNext href="/page/3" />
    </PaginationItem>
  </PaginationContent>
</Pagination>
```

---

### `Sidebar` family — ⚠️ "use client"

- **Import:** `import { Sidebar, SidebarProvider, SidebarHeader, SidebarContent, SidebarFooter, SidebarGroup, SidebarGroupLabel, SidebarGroupContent, SidebarMenuItem, SidebarMenuButton, SidebarTrigger, useSidebar } from "@modlin/ui/sidebar"`
- **Constraints:** **"use client"** — uses context (`SidebarContext`), `useState`, `useCallback`, and the `useMobile` hook. Wrap your sidebar in `SidebarProvider`; any component can then call `useSidebar()` to read/toggle state. On mobile (`< 640px`) the toggle uses the mobile-open state. `SidebarTrigger` renders a collapsible `Button`.
- **Quirks to be aware of:** `SidebarProps` declares a misspelled `collasped` prop that is ignored; `SidebarMenuButton` supports `selected` / `collapsed` to control the ghost-button variant and icon sizing.

**Props**

```ts
export interface SidebarProps extends ViewProps {
  collasped?: boolean      // NOTE: misspelled + ignored
  size?: "sm" | "lg"       // declared but not applied
}
export interface SidebarHeaderProps extends ViewProps {}
export interface SidebarContentProps extends ViewProps {}
export interface SidebarFooterProps extends ViewProps {}
export interface SidebarMenuItemProps extends ViewProps {}

export interface SidebarMenuButtonProps extends ButtonProps {
  selected?: boolean
  collapsed?: boolean      // renders icon-md variant when true
}

export interface SidebarGroupLabelProps extends Omit<LabelProps, "htmlFor"> {
  expanded?: boolean
  asChild?: boolean
}
export interface SidebarGroupContentProps extends ViewProps {
  expanded?: boolean       // hidden when false (default true)
  loading?: boolean        // renders skeleton menu item while true
}
export interface SidebarGroupProps {
  id?: string
  expanded?: boolean
  children?: ReactNode
  className?: string
}

export interface SidebarProviderProps {
  defaultOpen?: boolean                 // default true
  open?: boolean                        // controlled
  onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void
  children?: ReactNode
}

export interface SidebarContextProps {
  open: boolean
  setOpen(open: boolean): void
  openMobile: boolean
  setOpenMobile(open: boolean): void
  isMobile: boolean
  toggleSidebar(): void
}
export const SidebarContext = createContext<SidebarContextProps | null>(null)
export function useSidebar(): SidebarContextProps  // throws if used outside SidebarProvider
```

**Example**

```tsx
// app/components/app-sidebar.tsx ("use client")
import {
  SidebarProvider, Sidebar, SidebarHeader, SidebarContent, SidebarGroup,
  SidebarGroupLabel, SidebarGroupContent, SidebarMenuItem, SidebarMenuButton,
  SidebarTrigger,
} from "@modlin/ui/sidebar"
import { IconHome, IconUser } from "@tabler/icons-react"

export default function AppSidebar() {
  return (
    <SidebarProvider defaultOpen>
      <div className="flex h-screen">
        <Sidebar>
          <SidebarHeader>
            <SidebarTrigger />
          </SidebarHeader>
          <SidebarContent>
            <SidebarGroup>
              <SidebarGroupLabel>Menu</SidebarGroupLabel>
              <SidebarGroupContent>
                <SidebarMenuItem>
                  <SidebarMenuButton selected>
                    <IconHome /> Dashboard
                  </SidebarMenuButton>
                </SidebarMenuItem>
                <SidebarMenuItem>
                  <SidebarMenuButton>
                    <IconUser /> Profile
                  </SidebarMenuButton>
                </SidebarMenuItem>
              </SidebarGroupContent>
            </SidebarGroup>
          </SidebarContent>
        </Sidebar>
        <main className="flex-1 p-6">Page content</main>
      </div>
    </SidebarProvider>
  )
}
```

---

## 7. Disclosure / Accordion

### `Accordion` family

- **Import:** `import { Accordion, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger, AccordionContent } from "@modlin/ui/accordion"`
- **Constraints:** Server-safe. Built on native `<details>` / `<summary>`, so open/close state is browser-managed (no JS, works in Server Components). Items are **independent** (each `<details>` toggles on its own; not an exclusive accordion). `AccordionItem`'s `value` prop and `Accordion`'s `value`/`defaultValue` are declared but **not wired** to behavior. `AccordionContent` renders a `<p>` (text content only).

**Props**

```ts
export interface AccordionProps extends ViewProps {
  defaultValue?: string   // declared but unused
  value?: string          // declared but unused
}
export interface AccordionItemProps extends ViewProps {
  value?: string          // declared but unused
}
export interface AccordionTriggerProps extends ViewProps {}
export interface AccordionContentProps extends ViewProps {}
```

**Example**

```tsx
// app/components/faq.tsx (Server Component)
import { Accordion, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger, AccordionContent } from "@modlin/ui/accordion"

<Accordion className="max-w-lg">
  <AccordionItem>
    <AccordionTrigger>What is @modlin/ui?</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>A lightweight React UI library built on the Motive design system.</AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem>
    <AccordionTrigger>Is it themeable?</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>Yes — tokens are defined in globals.css and follow prefers-color-scheme.</AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>
```

---

### `Collapsible` family — ⚠️ "use client"

- **Import:** `import { Collapsible, CollapsibleTrigger, CollapsibleContent, useCollapsible } from "@modlin/ui/collapsible"`
- **Constraints:** **"use client"** — React context + `useState`. Controlled (`open` / `onOpenChange`) or uncontrolled (`defaultOpen`). `useCollapsible()` throws if used outside a `Collapsible`. `CollapsibleContent` returns `null` when closed.

**Props**

```ts
export interface CollapsibleProps {
  defaultOpen?: boolean
  open?: boolean
  onOpenChange?(open: boolean): void
  children?: ReactNode
}
export interface CollapsibleContext {
  open: boolean
  toggle(): void
}
// CollapsibleTrigger / CollapsibleContent accept ViewProps
```

**Example**

```tsx
// app/components/filter-section.tsx ("use client")
import { Collapsible, CollapsibleTrigger, CollapsibleContent } from "@modlin/ui/collapsible"

export default function FilterSection() {
  return (
    <Collapsible defaultOpen>
      <CollapsibleTrigger className="flex items-center gap-2 text-sm font-medium">
        Filters
      </CollapsibleTrigger>
      <CollapsibleContent className="mt-2">
        <p className="text-muted-foreground">Filter options…</p>
      </CollapsibleContent>
    </Collapsible>
  )
}
```

---

## 8. Data Display

### `Avatar` — ⚠️ "use client"

- **Import:** `import Avatar from "@modlin/ui/avatar"`
- **Constraints:** **"use client"** — uses `useState` to handle image errors. Built on `next/image` (`ImageProps`), so image hosting must be configured in `next.config` (remote patterns). When `src` is missing/errors, the `fallback` string is shown (first 3 characters, uppercased, mono font). `size` defaults to 32 (also used as the `next/image` width/height).

**Props**

```ts
export interface AvatarProps extends Omit<ImageProps, "src"> {
  src?: string | URL
  size?: number          // default 32
  fallback: string       // required
}
```

**Example**

```tsx
// app/components/user-avatar.tsx ("use client")
import Avatar from "@modlin/ui/avatar"

export function UserAvatar() {
  return <Avatar src="/avatars/alice.png" fallback="Alice Johnson" size={48} />
}
```

---

## 9. Hooks & Utilities

### `useMobile`

- **Import:** `import { useMobile } from "@modlin/ui/use-mobile"`
- **Constraints:** **Client-side hook** — uses `window.matchMedia` in `useEffect` (SSR-safe; initializes `false`). Breakpoint is `< 640px`. Returns `{ isMobile }`.

```ts
export function useMobile(): { isMobile: boolean }
```

**Example**

```tsx
// app/components/responsive-nav.tsx ("use client")
import { useMobile } from "@modlin/ui/use-mobile"

export default function ResponsiveNav() {
  const { isMobile } = useMobile()
  return <nav>{isMobile ? "Menu" : "Full navigation"}</nav>
}
```

---

## 10. Known Quirks & Gotchas (quick reference)

| Component | Quirk |
|---|---|
| `Button` | `loading` disables the button and injects a `Spinner`; `label` doubles as `aria-label` and `title`. |
| `Button` (asChild) | Clones the child; only the first child is used. |
| `Checkbox` | Visual state is a peer-linked button; controlled usage requires wiring `checked` + `onChange`. |
| `Switch` | Controlled via `checked`/`onChange`; input uses `name={props.id}` (not `name`). |
| `RadioGroup` | Default selection prop is `default`, not `defaultValue`. |
| `Select` (custom) | Experimental; prefers `select.native` for production. |
| `Select.native` | Styling relies on `@import "@modlin/ui/globals.css"` (base-select). |
| `Textarea` | `variant` prop is declared but not applied. |
| `Stack` | `direction` prop accepted but not applied; gaps are inline styles. |
| `Header` | `children` must be a `[Heading, Text]` tuple. |
| `Alert` | `dismissible` not implemented; `Alert.Destructive` is the destructive variant. |
| `toast` | Requires a `<div id="toasts">` mount point; client-only; `description` unused. |
| `PaginationNext` | Default label reads "Go to previous page" (library copy-paste quirk). |
| `Sidebar` | `collasped` prop is a misspelled no-op; use `SidebarProvider` + `useSidebar`. |
| `Avatar` | `next/image` — configure remote domains in `next.config`. |
| `Item` | Renders `<li>`; `PaginationItem` renders `<ul>` (nested-list quirk). |
| `Accordion` | Native `<details>`; items are independent, not mutually exclusive. |
| Icons | Components style `>svg` children (size 4–5). Use `@tabler/icons-react` for best results. |

---
